articles.title: Nonprofit wants to launch 80,000-year mission to Alpha Centauri in 2029 (video)
articles.excerpt: The Fermi Explorer Mission plans to launch a small, cheap probe to Alpha Centauri in the next few years, to inspire further exploration and help humanity contemplate its place in the universe.
articles.body: The first dedicated mission to another star will launch before the end of the decade, if all goes according to plan. A nonprofit called the Fermi Explorer Mission announced today (Sept. 1) that it plans to send a small probe toward Alpha Centauri by 2029. But none of us will live to see the interstellar spacecraft 's historic arrival; its journey is expected to take about 80,000 years. "We hope to be both the first to leave and the last to arrive at Alpha Centauri," Philip Johnston, co-founder and president of the Fermi Explorer Mission, said in a statement today. "None of us will be here when this journey ends, and that is the point.

articles.title: Why Enterprise AI Fails: The Hidden Trap of Pure Probabilistic LLMs and the Rise of Neuro-Symbolic Architecture
articles.excerpt: The modern enterprise software landscape sits at a precarious crossroads. For the past few years, the narrative around artificial intelligence has been dominated by neural scaling laws. We have watche…
articles.body: The modern enterprise software landscape sits at a precarious crossroads. For the past few years, the narrative around artificial intelligence has been dominated by neural scaling laws. We have watched Large Language Models (LLMs) scale from niche research projects into trillion-parameter juggernauts capable of writing code, summarizing massive legal briefs, and holding surprisingly nuanced conversations. Yet, as engineering teams push these models out of sandboxed chat interfaces and into mission-critical enterprise workflows—spanning financial ledger reconciliation, clinical diagnostic routing, regulatory compliance auditing, and automated supply chain execution—a harsh reality is setting in. Pure probabilistic LLMs are fundamentally unsuited for mission-critical enterprise systems.

articles.title: Codex with ChatGPT Splits Planning From Execution
articles.excerpt: Codex with ChatGPT, a public GitHub project, routes planning and code review to the ChatGPT web app while retaining Codex as the agent that edits files, runs shell commands and executes tests. For dev…
articles.body: Codex with ChatGPT , a public GitHub project, routes planning and code review to the ChatGPT web app while retaining Codex as the agent that edits files, runs shell commands and executes tests. For developers, the practical aim is to use an existing ChatGPT web subscription for reasoning without replacing the Codex-based execution harness. A read-only handoff between the two agents The project describes a local C2C Bridge between ChatGPT and a workspace. Codex and ChatGPT exchange small structured state messages for the plan, execution and review loop, while ChatGPT retrieves repository context through nine read-only MCP tools, including file reads, workspace search, Git status and diffs, and test-status and execution-output records.

articles.body: A nonprofit organization called the Fermi Explorer Mission announced today that it intends to launch a spacecraft to our nearest star system by the end of 2029.  It’s a hugely ambitious mission—if all goes well, the spacecraft could take up to 80,000 years to arrive at Alpha Centauri, which is 4.4 light-years away. And the spacecraft will follow a novel trajectory discovered by an AI system developed by Physical Superintelligence (PSI), an AI physics research lab. PSI is launching today with $58 million in funding led by Breakthrough Energy, a climate-focused investment group founded by Microsoft cofounder Bill Gates. It’s not the first time this has been tried.

articles.title: On this day in space! Sept. 1, 1979: NASA's Pioneer 11 probe becomes 1st spacecraft to visit Saturn
articles.excerpt: On Sept. 1, 1979, NASA's robotic space probe Pioneer 11 became the first spacecraft to fly by Saturn. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Sept. 1, 1979, NASA's robotic space probe Pioneer 11 became the first spacecraft to fly by Saturn . Pioneer 11 launched in 1973 on a mission to explore the asteroid belt, Jupiter and Saturn. It launched directly toward Jupiter , then used Jupiter's gravity to slingshot around the planet, make a sharp turn and start flying toward Saturn. Four years and nine months later, it finally made it to Saturn . During its closest approach, it was about 13,000 miles (2,100 kilometers) above the planet's cloud tops. Because NASA's two Voyager probes were also on their way to Saturn at that point, they sent Pioneer 11 straight through Saturn's rings so it could determine whether it was safe for the Voyagers to do the same thing years down the road.

articles.title: Why do black hole flares die out? It may be down to how stars spin
articles.excerpt: Some stars encounter supermassive black holes and live to tell the tale. New research shows why the flares these encounters cause dim over repeated episodes.
articles.body: Some stars encounter supermassive black holes and live to tell the tale. New research shows why the flares these encounters cause dim over repeated episodes, and it may be down to the way these stars spin and an escaping binary partner that leaves them to be a stellar snack for a black hole. Some stars are unfortunate enough to encounter the supermassive black holes that sit at the heart of every galaxy, being subjected to immense tidal forces that turn them into a strand of stellar spaghetti, a process called " spaghettification ." This plasma pasta wraps around the black hole and is gradually fed to it, with some former star stuff being ejected as near-light-speed jets. These occurrences are called tidal disruption events (TDEs).

articles.title: NASA's Roman Space Telescope is just one of a few missions named after real-life women
articles.excerpt: NASA's Roman space telescope, which launched on Aug. 30, is part of a small set of missions named after female historical figures.
articles.body: NASA's next big space telescope is not only meant to unlock some of the mysteries of dark energy. It also is a pioneer in the naming of missions. Scientific American recently said that the observatory, which launched on Aug. 30 , is the first ever space telescope ever named after a real-life woman: American astronomer Nancy Grace Roman , who supported development of the iconic Hubble Space Telescope and was NASA's first head of astronomy in the 1960s. articles.title: 5 planets will light up the September sky — here's how to see them
articles.excerpt: Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn are all visible this September. Here's when and where to look.
articles.body: Venus, which has been such a prominent object in the western evening twilight sky since the start of spring, is now entering its final full month of visibility. With each passing day, it drops a bit lower in the southwest sky and sets a bit earlier and closer to the vicinity of the sun. By month’s end, making a Venus sighting will be rather difficult as it will be following the sun to below the horizon by only about 30 minutes. During the last week of September, Mercury pops up above the western horizon at dusk, primarily for those living in the southern half of the U.S., though you might need Venus to help direct you to this rocky little world.
